business_rules.statement: Every cell in every permission matrix carries an explicit status from the closed set; blank cells are prohibited, because a blank cell is an unanswered question.
Where a matrix and a card appear to disagree, the card governs and the matrix is the defect.

The five tenant roles are fixed at V1; scopes of Tenant, Site, and Area are held simultaneously and orthogonally; multi-role is additive with the audit log recording identity and action rather than 'acting as role'.
A Tenant Admin has no platform authority, there is no Tenant Super Admin, and the two are distinct security domains.
business_rules.applies_to: tenant roles vs platform console roles

business_rules.statement: No tenant role can create any execution record below the Run.
business_rules.applies_to: Step Execution, Data Capture, Unit Execution

business_rules.statement: The Read-only Auditor holds no write capability anywhere and no Client Command Center access at all.
Hold release resolves to Quality Manager only in every matrix, every card, and every interface.
Platform console roles hold no tenant operational authority outside a named access class.
business_rules.applies_to: Root Super Admin, Admin, Platform Engineer, Support

business_rules.statement: On a device, cached authority is trusted only within the credential-trust window of approximately 24 hours with a 72-hour ceiling; beyond it the device blocks new work rather than trusting stale authority.
The device is authoritative for what happened and never for what is permitted.
An untrusted device timestamp never orders a write; outside the skew threshold the write routes to Quality Manager resolution rather than winning.
No artificial-intelligence capability holds write access to evidence, audit events, holds, classifications, access-class records, or erasure certificates.
Every artificial-intelligence write in the matrix names the human gate that bounds it; removing the gate causes the write to be refused.
Procedural memory is written only by publication, never by an agent.
No object in the catalog is purged; every retention row resolves to tiering, supersession, anonymisation, or the named-standard exception.
Anonymisation executes at most once per subject, proven by an effect receipt, and never in Regulated-Industry mode.
A legal hold in force blocks both tiering and compliance-driven deletion for its scope.
business_rules.enforcement_point: legal-hold check inside the erasure workflow

business_rules.statement: The platform is delivered as exactly one web application presenting exactly four role-gated web surfaces, plus exactly one separate native mobile application.
Surface separation is enforced by a server-side authorisation decision per request against roles and Tenant, Site, and Area scopes; a request outside scope is refused, not filtered.
No user interface element anywhere in the product presents Tenant Administration as a sixth surface.
The Frontline Worker Application executes a complete run with the network disabled for the whole run, including gates, detection, severity classification, and containment launch.
No web surface can reach a device except through a Delivery Operations Hub service and the command channel.
business_rules.enforcement_point: TEST-ARCH-006 static analysis fails the build

business_rules.statement: An administrative or operational change and its audit event commit in the same transaction, so an action that cannot be audited does not happen.
The Client Command Center displays an as-of freshness marker on every live view, at all times, including when the view is current.
A run whose work package is not ready cannot be started, and the Frontline Worker Application states the reason in plain language.
A permission may be scoped away by role, but a prohibition holds for every role including the most privileged; the Command Center's four absolute exclusions are absolute, for every role.
The Frontline Worker Application never displays another worker's data, and never displays a pace, timer, or performance measure.
The Hub is delivered as nineteen modules, thirteen in Band A and six in Band B, all in V1 scope.
The Delivery Operations Hub originates no operational data; every capture in the Hub carries a Frontline origin and a runtime envelope.
The Delivery Operations Hub runs no live agents.
No Workflow content is publishable without passing Author, then a different Reviewer, then the Release Authority.
A measurement screen cannot be saved without at least one severity mapping.
Publication is blocked where the English or Spanish locale is incomplete.
A republish without a republish description is refused, and the description appears on the first screen of the next execution.
The Client Command Center holds no database and no configuration of its own.
The operational action set is exactly ten; no eleventh action is reachable by any role.
Every hold displays its lifecycle honestly as issued, propagating, or in force per device.
A committed value is immutable; a correction creates an appended annotation record carrying who, when, and what changed, and the original remains readable.
Captured media never appears in the device gallery or in any operating-system-shared store.
Sync state is always visible and never described with a single undifferentiated word.
Exactly one Root Super Admin account exists and cannot be created through any user interface.
A Platform Engineer's mutating change never applies without an Admin approval.
Record-level tenant operational content is reachable only through one of the three named access classes; no ambient browsing path exists.
A looser-than-floor value is rejected and not written; the rejection states the bound.
No control exists anywhere in the screen group that could remove any part of the Severity 1 minimum action bundle.
Where a bound cannot be read, the change is refused rather than applied.
No Studio action creates, alters, or removes an atom, a core agent definition, a memory store type, or an evaluation-harness rule.
No Command Center action changes a configured value except through the governed Lane-B pipeline.
A composed agent cannot act on any floor until the tenant approval chain, the evaluation gate, and platform review have all passed.
Only reasoning agents may be composed by tenants at V1; no composition path produces an action agent.
An emergency pause never suppresses on-device gates, specification checks, severity classification, or the Severity 1 hold.
The compliance-emergency path is the only write route into tenant data from the platform side, and requires two authorisations.
Every capture event carries every field of the runtime envelope; a capture missing any field is rejected with a recorded reason.
The command channel carries exactly the five classes and no sixth class is expressible.
No surface shows a command as applied before the device has acknowledged it.
A capture is never discarded; every terminal state other than officially recorded retains the item and a recorded reason.
The pinned workflow version in the envelope is the version pinned at assignment, never the current published version.
Named-location provenance is expressed in the tenant's own hierarchy names and is never a coordinate and never used as a gate.
An operational event never satisfies a gate, never triggers a classification, and never enters the Execution Summary as a measurement.
The placing of a Severity 1 hold on the capturing device never depends on the command channel.
The worker-facing compliance suspension message is exactly the fixed text and is not localised away or reworded.
No surface displays a state it has not confirmed; unknown renders as unknown with the time state was last known.
A notification is never the sole mechanism enforcing a hold, a qualification, an authorisation, an approval, a suspension, or a device command.
Agent unavailability renders as unavailability, never as silence or as an empty result.
A looser-than-floor value is rejected and not written; the platform never logs and applies it.
Every configurable setting in the product has a registry entry carrying a default, a bound, and a direction of strictness.
Platform-fixed items present no control anywhere, including no disabled control.
No release re-bases an in-flight run; a run finishes on the workflow version it started on.
A mobile application update never discards, alters, or endangers locally held captures.
Exactly one service writes each record type.
The rule set applied to a record type is identical regardless of the surface an action originates from.
No reading surface persists an authoritative copy of a record it does not own.
A worker cannot produce, alter, or attest to their own qualification record on any surface.
Refusals are recorded, and absence of an authorisation decision results in refusal.
The audit log has no mutation path on any surface for any role.

Artificial intelligence may never elevate its permissions, change tenant scope, impersonate a role, self-approve, release a Severity 1 hold, bypass a gate, classify deviations, execute stale queued actions, delete evidence or audit history, or make an offline device appear remotely controlled.
A new entry point to an existing service is permitted; a new writer for an existing record type is prohibited.
Adding a Command Center action beyond the closed set of ten is a scope decision, never a drift, and carries the price stated in section 6.14.4.

failures_fallbacks.trigger: A matrix and a card disagree, or a cell is blank
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: The card governs and the matrix is corrected
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Where the card itself is silent, the cell becomes Client Decision Required with a DEC-* identifier rather than a guess
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: An explicitly unanswered cell
failures_fallbacks.recovery: The decision lands and both card and matrix update together

failures_fallbacks.trigger: An authority check cannot be evaluated, or a role grant has been revoked but has not reached a device
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: The strictest interpretation applies — the action is refused
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Beyond the credential-trust window the device blocks new work rather than trusting stale authority
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: Refusal, with the reason stated
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Re-evaluation at reconnection, with revocations arriving on the command channel

failures_fallbacks.trigger: A value is found in two places with different content
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: The authoritative holder from the source-of-truth matrix wins and the other copy is refreshed
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Where authority cannot be determined — the skew case — the value is quarantined and routed to the Quality Manager
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: A quarantined value, visibly flagged, excluded from summaries
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Resolution and append; audited recompute with the prior computed output preserved

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Tiering scheduler does not run; anonymisation scheduler runs twice; erasure collides with a legal hold; an agent attempts a prohibited write
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Data stays hot, which costs storage and risks nothing, because nothing is purged
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Where a legal hold is in force, erasure does not execute and no certificate is issued
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: Data retained, identity intact, act not performed, with the condition visible
failures_fallbacks.recovery: The scheduler resumes and reconciliation reports the gap

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Loss of the web application; authorisation service unavailability
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Devices already holding pinned work packages continue executing offline; captures accumulate committed locally then queued
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: If the web application returns but Hub services remain unavailable, the Command Center renders nothing actionable
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The floor continues on pinned packages under local gates; no oversight surface displays stale data as current; new assignments cannot be made
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Devices drain their upload queues in order; late captures fold in flagged late_arrival, else audited recompute

failures_fallbacks.trigger: A broken link in the interaction chain (Studio-to-Frontline, Hub-to-Command-Center, or the command channel)
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Package readiness state shown as not ready; board renders last state with a freshness marker; commands held centrally as created, authorized, queued, available for delivery
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Package readiness never resolves so the run cannot start; staleness exceeds tolerance so the board degrades to explicit not-live; the device never returns so the command never advances
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: Run does not start; oversight explicitly unavailable; floor continues under its local deterministic layer with the command pending and visible as pending
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Package build retry at next sync; board refresh on link restore; pending commands download and apply in order at next device sync

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Charter erosion — a capability built on a surface whose charter forbids it
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: The capability is refactored to execute through the owning surface's service
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: If the refactor is not possible within the release, the capability is withdrawn rather than shipped
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The capability does not exist
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Records written outside the owning service are replayed through it under an audited correction, originals preserved append-only

failures_fallbacks.trigger: The Hub cannot accept a write — persistence unavailable, audit write cannot commit, validation dependency unavailable
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: The write is refused and the calling surface states plainly the change was not made; no optimistic UI state
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: If the outage persists across a shift boundary, no new assignments can be made for the incoming shift
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The floor completes work already assigned under local gates and stops at the boundary of what was assigned; no paper workaround inside the product
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Queued device captures drain in order; late captures fold in flagged late_arrival; after finish, audited recompute

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Authoring or publication unavailable; locale check cannot run; package build fails after publication
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Authoring stops; no offline authoring mode exists or is proposed; the floor is unaffected on pinned packages
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: A published version exists but is not distributable; the Hub must not assign runs against it
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: Runs continue on the last successfully packaged version; new assignments referencing the unbuildable version are refused; no silent version substitution
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Package build retries; re-pinning only by cancelling and re-creating the assignment as an audited act

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Refresh fails; an action submission fails; an agent produces nothing
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: The board holds its last successful state behind an explicit as-of marker and continues attempting refresh
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Past the staleness tolerance the board renders an explicit not-live state and operational actions are refused
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: Oversight explicitly unavailable; the floor unaffected; every hold retains its last known propagation state with its as-of time
failures_fallbacks.recovery: On restore the board refreshes from Hub records; nothing on this surface requires reconciliation

failures_fallbacks.trigger: The device loses connectivity mid-run; prolonged offline beyond the trust window; clock skew; storage pressure
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: The run continues offline in full; captures accumulate committed locally then queued, shown in plain language
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Storage full on the device — behaviour explicitly deferred, carried as DEC-STORE-001
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The worker completes what the pinned package allows under local gates and stops where a gate blocks; held captures remain in the encrypted store undeleted and unaltered
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Captures advance to officially recorded, reflected in summaries, reconciled; conflicts become sync-conflict records the worker never sees

failures_fallbacks.trigger: The console is unavailable; approval service unavailable; the evaluation harness unavailable
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Tenant surfaces and the floor continue on the configuration already in force; no platform change can be made
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: If the evaluation harness is unavailable, nothing agentic may be published — that is the gate working
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The platform runs on its last approved definition; an active emergency pause stays active until a separate audited resume
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Submitted-but-unapproved changes remain submitted; none applies silently on restore; each is re-presented with its original submission time

failures_fallbacks.trigger: A tenant setting cannot be validated because the tenant-configuration registry is unreachable
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: The change is refused; the current value remains in force unchanged
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: If the registry stays unreachable, no tenant setting can be changed for the duration
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The tenant runs on its last validated configuration; operations unaffected
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Registry reachable and a bound successfully read; refused attempts are recorded

failures_fallbacks.trigger: A tier boundary is crossed by a shipped capability
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: The offending capability is refused at the authorisation layer and the attempt is recorded
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: If a boundary crossing has already shipped, it is withdrawn, not fenced with a warning
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The capability does not exist at the wrong tier
failures_fallbacks.recovery: State created by a boundary-crossing action is replayed through the correct tier's service under an audited correction

failures_fallbacks.trigger: A composed agent fails a gate — approval chain declines, evaluation scenarios fail, or platform review declines
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: The composition returns to the author with the failing gate and its reason named
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Repeated evaluation failure means the composition is withdrawn rather than exempted
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The composed agent does not exist on any floor; the tenant continues with the three pre-built agents
failures_fallbacks.recovery: None required; the failed attempt and its evaluation results are retained for audit

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Pressure on the Tier-1 boundary — informal per-tenant exception, floor changed without root approval, invariant bypassed through support
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: The request is refused, recorded, and routed to the client's platform leadership as a product decision
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: An existing per-tenant exception is withdrawn and the tenant notified
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The platform-fixed behaviour applies; a tenant that cannot accept it is a commercial conversation
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Records produced under an improper exception are identified and annotated append-only; originals never altered

failures_fallbacks.trigger: The spine degrades — no connectivity, partial upload, validation failure, command rejected, device never returns
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Queue and retry, with back-pressure if the queue grows
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: A device that never returns leaves captures unreconciled and commands undelivered (DEC-WIPE-001)
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The floor is protected by the local deterministic layer; central records show last contact, pending counts, propagation state and no more
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Captures fold into the run record while the finish window is open flagged late_arrival; commands reconcile on acknowledgement

failures_fallbacks.trigger: An envelope cannot be completed — unresolvable pinned version, missing provenance, missing device identity, missing limits
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: The capture does not complete and the worker is told which element is missing in plain language
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: If the package is structurally incomplete, the run cannot proceed at all; there is no degraded capture mode
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: No capture exists; the step is not marked complete; nothing is recorded as having happened
failures_fallbacks.recovery: None required for the failed capture; the failure is recorded as an operational event

failures_fallbacks.trigger: An operational event is lost or misclassified as a capture, or used to influence a classification
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: A malformed operational event is quarantined with a recorded reason and never blocks a worker
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Sustained loss degrades the Shift Handoff Agent's brief and Lane A signal quality; the brief must say so
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: Captures and classifications unaffected; context is thinner and labelled as thinner
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Events drain from the queue on reconnection and file with their original device timestamps

failures_fallbacks.trigger: A command cannot be delivered or applied — device offline indefinitely, rejected on device, superseded, or expired
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: The command remains available for delivery and is retried at every sync opportunity, shown as pending with last-contact time
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: The device never returns; DEC-WIPE-001 names this precisely and nothing is invented for any command class
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The floor operates under the state the device already holds; a pending hold release means the hold remains in force on that device
failures_fallbacks.recovery: On the device's return, pending commands apply in order; a superseded command is recorded as superseded rather than silently dropped

failures_fallbacks.trigger: The honest state itself cannot be determined — acknowledgement telemetry, last-contact tracking, or provider status unavailable
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: The surface displays 'state unknown' with the time state was last known and names what is unknown
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Operational actions whose safety argument rests on propagation are refused rather than taken blind
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The floor continues under its local deterministic layer; oversight explicitly states what it does not know; no report presents unknown state as settled
failures_fallbacks.recovery: State catches up from the acknowledgement record; reports produced during the unknown period are visibly superseded under audited recompute

failures_fallbacks.trigger: The floor cannot be enforced — floor register unreadable, a setting with no registry entry, or a direction recorded incorrectly
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Refuse the change and state that the bound cannot currently be confirmed
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: If a wrong direction has already permitted a looser value, revert to the last known-good value, notify the tenant, annotate affected records append-only
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The tenant runs on the platform default for the affected setting
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Refused attempts recorded; reverted values audited with their reason

failures_fallbacks.trigger: A release goes wrong — web release degrades surfaces, mobile release degrades execution, content publication produces an unbuildable package
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Roll back the web release; all four surfaces roll back together
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: A mobile release already on devices that cannot be rolled back; devices continue executing pinned packages
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The floor executes on pinned content under local gates; oversight may be degraded and says so; no data is lost
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Queued captures drain; late captures fold in flagged late_arrival; summaries carry as-of stamps and are visibly superseded if recomputed

failures_fallbacks.trigger: An ownership question cannot be answered, or two services are found writing one record type
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: The record type is assigned an owner by applying the origination rule and the second writer is removed
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: If the second writer cannot be removed within the release, the capability it serves is withdrawn rather than shipped
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The record type has one writer or the capability does not exist
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Records written by the removed writer are replayed through the owning service under an audited correction

failures_fallbacks.trigger: A seam produces a duplicate record — a reading surface treats its cache as authoritative
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Invalidate the cache and re-read from the owning service
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: If a surface cannot re-read, it must show the record as stale with its as-of time and refuse actions whose safety depends on current state
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The reading surface shows what it knows with its as-of time; the owning record is untouched
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Re-read on restore; no cache reconciliation is needed because a cache holds no truth

failures_fallbacks.trigger: A mutation is attempted outside the stated authority — role out of scope, surface reaching a service it should not, or an AI component attempting a mutation
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Refuse, record, and tell the acting person plainly what authority is required and who holds it
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: If the authorisation decision cannot be made, refuse; absence of a decision is never permission
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: No mutation occurs; the record is unchanged; the attempt is auditable
failures_fallbacks.recovery: None required; repeated refusals are a monitoring signal usually meaning a role or scope is misconfigured
